- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction.
- If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) or zero, model often underestimates; apply upward bias correction.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 90), model frequently overcorrects and overshoots; reduce forecast slope by 10–15% in next 5–7 days.
- When true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 80), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with recent low trend.
- If forecast is flat or rising slowly but true outcome shows rapid decline, model misses downward momentum; reduce forecast by 5–10% for next 3–5 days.
- Sentiment spikes to 1.00 followed by 0.00/0.33 often precedes sharp drop; model fails to anticipate; add early downward adjustment.
- For 30-day horizon, if forecast is >90 and true outcome drops below 85 within 10 days, model is overconfident; cap forecast at 90–92 for next 5 days.
